newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT DRIFTS SIDEWAYS, GAS OIL STUCK ON SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT DRIFTS SIDEWAYS, GAS OIL STUCK ON SUPPORT.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures drifted lower on Friday in thin volume while weak gas oil was stuck just above psychological $170 support.
Brokers said both markets were looking for fresh direction and some saw support coming later today in the form of pre-weekend short-covering against oversold NYMEX crude and products futures.
By 1215 GMT the September Brent contract stood nine cents down at $18.81 a barrel after unconvincingly easing through initial support around $18.80 earlier. Gas oil was off $2 at $170.50 a tonne.
Underlying sentiment remained positive despite the short term bearishness stirred by the impending Iraqi crude sale.

"While the physical crude markets generally are now affected by the prospects of Iraqi barrels hitting the market in the near future, nearby demand has not simply disappeared for good," Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report.
Iraqi crude sales aside, some analysts said the Brent market was looking overbought and due for a correction, but in the longer term they thought that the markets current uptrend will prevail.
They said if Brent can hold and consolidate above $18.40 over the weekend then the uptrend remains intact and there is still plenty of room for it to go higher again.
